newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan not yet ready to name a deputy, U.N. says.
newsitem.headline: Annan not yet ready to name a deputy, U.N. says.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan is not yet ready to announce the appointment of a deputy and would have to obtain General Assembly approval to create the post, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said on Wednesday.

Asked about a report from Oslo that Annan had asked former Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland to become deputy secretary-general, he said: "He's had discussions with her. But the short answer is he has nothing to announce yet.

"In the first place, the post of deputy does not yet exist in the U.N. budget, and so his intention to name a deputy would have to be preceded by a request to the General Assembly to approve the post," Eckhard said.
He acknowledged that Annan would prefer to name a woman as deputy secretary-general.

The person chosen would "assist him in his activities as secretary-general across the board ... someone that, when he has to travel, he can feel comfortable leaving behind the daily work of the organisation to that person," he said.

There has also been speculation that Brundtland, a physician, might want to head the World Health Organisation when its current director-general, Hiroshi Nakajima of Japan, ends his second five-year term in 1998.
